articles.description: The Iraqi prime minister called on foreign firms specializing in airport management and operations to invest in Mosul International Airport. An aerial view of Mosul International Airport’s design. Photo: 4b architects Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on foreign firms specializing in airport management and operations to invest in Mosul International Airport and develop its services. Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his visit on Monday to the city of Mosul to launch the Watan Initiative (Homeland Initiative), a nationwide housing and development program aiming to tackle the country’s housing crisis, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA). Mosul International Airport, according to al-Zaidi, is more than just a service project; it is a critical gateway for the province and Iraq as a whole. “We do not want the participating companies to merely construct a service terminal; rather, we want them to collaborate in turning the airport into an important service landmark,” al-Zaidi said. Mosul International Airport, which was previously destroyed by ISIS terrorists, is the third most important airport in Iraq, following Baghdad International Airport and Basra International Airport. December 2, 2007, marked the airport’s reopening following substantial runway and facility upgrades. It was first created as a civil airport in 1990. The airport became a key military site after it was overrun by the terrorist organization ISIS in June 2014. They held it until the Iraqi army took it back on February 23, 2017. Following its liberation, Mosul International Airport underwent renovations. By November 2019, de-mining activities were finished, and plans for a thorough reconstruction were initiated. To complete the airport’s renovation, the Iraqi government inked contracts with SEA Milan Airports and Aeroports de Paris Ingenierie in December 2020. Rehabilitating the northern Iraqi airport is considered critical for improving regional connections and assisting the local economy’s revival after years of conflict.

articles.description: عامة علاوي والعبودي يؤكدان اهمية تعزيز حضور المؤسسات الفكرية في ترسيخ الوعي المعرفي والحوار البناء الأربعاء 14 , تشرين الأول 2026 21:04 | عامة | عدد القراءات : 503 بغداد / نينا/ اكد النائب مهدي تقي آمرلي ،رئيس كتلة بدر النيابية ، ان اكمال الكابينة الوزارية ، سيتم الاسبوع المقبل ، وبصيغة مختلفة عن التصويت على الكابينة الوزارية في المرحلة الاولى . وقال آمرلي في تصريح للوكالة الوطنية العراقية للانباء / نينا/:" ان الاسبوع الحالي لن يشهد التصويت على المتبقي السبت 10 , تشرين الأول 2026 12:26 بغداد /نينا/ اصدرت هيئة الإعلام والاتصالات إعماماً الى المؤسسات الاعلامية كافة بشأن التغطية المسؤولة للمستجدات الاقتصادية وتعديل سعر الصرف . ودعت الهيئة الى اعتماد الدقة في كل ما ينشر ويبث بشأن سعر الصرف والأسواق والرواتب، والتحقق منه من مصادره المختصة قبل النشر، وعرض القرار بأسبابه ودوافعه وآثا السبت 10 , تشرين الأول 2026 11:27 بغداد/نينا/أعلنت هيئة النزاهة الاتحاديَّة عن الإطاحة بشبكةٍ تضمُّ مُوظَّفين في مُديريَّة تربية الرصافة الأولى تمارس أعمال الاحتيال والتزوير. و أشارت الهيئة في معرض حديثها عن العمليَّـة التي نُفِّذَت بموجب مذكراتٍ قضائيّةٍ، إلى رصد شبكةٍ تضمُّ (١٢) مُوظَّفاً تقوم بالاحتيال على المواطنين ووعدهم با الجمعة 09 , تشرين الأول 2026 11:42

articles.description: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Basim Mohammed Khudair, Iraq’s Minister of Oil, attended a series of high-level energy meetings in Riyadh, including OPEC+ consultations and international ministerial talks on oil market stability, […] Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Basim Mohammed Khudair, Iraq’s Minister of Oil, attended a series of high-level energy meetings in Riyadh, including OPEC+ consultations and international ministerial talks on oil market stability, energy security, and investment amidst rising regional instability. According to Iraq’s Ministry of Oil, Khudair attended an OPEC+ consultative meeting where members addressed global oil market changes, energy security, and the significance of continuing to invest in oil infrastructure. The talks also focused on the need to fortify energy systems and infrastructure to survive interruptions, as regional instability and uncertainty over shipping via the Strait of Hormuz continue to provide issues for oil-producing nations. Iraq, one of OPEC’s main producers, depends largely on petroleum exports to fund government expenditures; therefore, the stability of international oil markets and export routes is critical to its economy. During his visit to Riyadh, Khudair attended the 25th WPC Energy Congress, themed “Pathways to Energy for All.” The congress gathered energy ministers, industry leaders, and international organizations to discuss energy security, investment, and the transition to more sustainable energy systems. The discussions included technology to minimize carbon emissions, clean hydrogen development, and energy project finance, as well as initiatives to ensure secure and dependable energy supply. The Iraqi Minister also attended the 17th International Energy Forum Ministerial Meeting (IEF17), which was sponsored by Saudi Arabia with the subject “Energy Security and Shared Goals in a New Era.” The event aimed to increase collaboration between energy producers and consumers, improve openness in global oil and gas markets, and expand energy data sharing. Participants also spoke about the Joint Organizations Data Initiative (JODI), an international initiative to increase the availability and reliability of energy market data. The discussions took place in Riyadh as Saudi Arabia hosted a series of big international energy summits, bringing together governments and business executives at a time when the Gulf region’s security worries are high. Al-Ibadi’s involvement was part of Iraq’s overall political and economic engagement with Saudi Arabia, which included conversations with Iraqi Minister of Electricity Ali Saadi Waheeb about bilateral energy cooperation and electrical infrastructure. The visit also coincided with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s trip in Riyadh, underlining ongoing high-level cooperation between Baghdad and Riyadh as both nations deal with regional security and economic issues.
